recognize_zh: 一團大型細胞，細胞質豐富、淡藍灰色，帶有細纖維條紋狀（皺紙樣）紋理，核小而圓、偏心且染色質粗，這是典型 Gaucher 細胞。
features: Clustered large cells, several times the diameter of adjacent hematopoietic cells
Abundant pale blue-gray cytoplasm with fine fibrillary striations (crumpled tissue paper appearance)
Small, round to oval, often eccentric nuclei with coarse clumped chromatin
Some cells multinucleated or with overlapping nuclei
Occasional clear vacuoles; background marrow cells and red cells at the edges
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of large macrophages with abundant pale blue-gray cytoplasm displaying a fine fibrillary, wrinkled tissue paper texture. Nuclei are small, round to oval and eccentrically placed, with coarse chromatin; some cells appear binucleated. There are no discrete cytoplasmic granules or uniform foamy vacuolation. Findings are consistent with Gaucher cells, and confirmation with glucocerebrosidase enzyme activity or GBA1 genotyping is recommended.

ddx.vs: Pseudo-Gaucher cells mimic this appearance in CML, myeloma, thalassemia and other high-turnover states, and are distinguished by normal glucocerebrosidase activity and the underlying disease.
Niemann-Pick cells have evenly foamy, soap-bubble vacuolated cytoplasm instead of fibrillary striations.
Histiocytes stuffed with atypical mycobacteria show negative-image rods and are acid-fast positive.
Megakaryocytes have a large lobulated nucleus and granular pink cytoplasm, not small eccentric nuclei with striated blue cytoplasm.
